To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spatial and temporal pattern of MN PCD reflects their birth date and position along the rostrocaudocaudal axis of the developing spinal cord.

the spatial-temporal gradient observed for naturally occurring PCD in lumbar MNs of the chick embryo is related to the timing of prior exit from cell division and position within the developing lateral motor column.
MNs born earlier die earlier and are located more rostraly in the spinal cord, whereas those born later die later and are located more caudally.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and function of the nervous system.
the regulation of programmed cell death in developing spinal motoneurons, which is a critical event in the development of the nervous system.
the mechanisms underlying the death of spinal motor neurons during embryonic development and the factors regulating the survival and growth of spinal motor neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MNs generated in successive time intervals die in a spatial-temporal gradient, and this pattern is related to the time of prior cell cycle exit.
MNs die in a rostro-caudal gradient and that the rostrocaudally ordered MNs die in an age-dependent manner.
the spatial-temporal gradient observed in the naturally occurring PCD of lumbar MNs is a direct consequence of their time of exit and position within the developing spinal cord.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time at which a MN is born is a major determinant for when it will die during the PCD period.

MNs generated during successive intervals of cell cycle exit die at progressively later times during the PCD period, and the rostrocaudally progressive nature of MN PCD can be accounted for by the earlier born MNs dying sooner and being located rostral to those born later.
the time of MN generation and the time of death of the same cell population are related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the timing of MN death during the period of PCC is not arbitrary.
the time of birth of MNs and their subsequent time of death are linked.
the time that MNs exit the cell cycle is an important determinant of their survival.
